requirement_text.REQ-432:
Follow-on to REQ-373 (service_catalog version/status lifecycle + real PinResolver.Lookup, status: done on the backend) and to REQ-399 (case-detail dependency-version/provenance screen, status: done -- REQ-399 already built the GET /api/v1/instances/{id}/pins route, web/src/hooks/useInstancePins.ts, and web/src/components/instances/InstancePinsPanel.tsx, wired into InstanceDetailPage.tsx). Filed from ISS-0898, split from ISS-0890's WF05-FULL-20260929 PLATFORM UAT report: the platform-instance-pin-survives-catalog-change scenario (test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/platform/instance-pin-survives-catalog-change.yaml) is BLOCKED not because the read-only provenance screen is missing (REQ-399 built that) but because two operator ACTIONS the scenario's own steps exercise have no UI anywhere, and REQ-399's own SCOPE explicitly excluded one of them: "any UI affordance to CHANGE a pin from this screen... is a separate requirement if one is ever filed."
WHAT EXISTS TODAY, verified 2026-09-30 by direct source read: - `POST /api/v1/admin/services/:service_id/versions` (publish) and
  `POST /api/v1/admin/services/:service_id/retire` (retire) are real,
  shipped REQ-373 routes (lib/letflow/routers/admin_services.ex,
  design doc lib/letflow/design/req373-service-catalog-version-lifecycle.md
  §7), gated by the existing :AdminServicesManage permission. Grepping
  web/src/api/services.ts and web/src/pages/admin/services/ServicesPage.tsx
  for "publish"/"retire"/"version" returns zero hits beyond the existing
  `ServiceRecord` type -- neither route has any frontend client function or
  UI control. An operator today cannot publish a new service-connection
  version or retire an old one from the GUI at all, which is exactly the
  scenario's own step 2 action.
- `POST /instances/:id/rebind-pins` is a real, shipped REQ-078/PIN-05 route
  (lib/letflow/routers/instances.ex, `Letflow.Engine.PinRebind.rebind_pins/3`,
  200 response `{instance_id, changes, rebound_at}`, each change item
  carrying `ref`/`prior_version`/`new_version` per the
  `INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND` event it appends). Grepping web/src for "rebind"
  returns zero hits beyond REQ-399's own read-only provenance panel and its
  test -- there is no rebind client function, no rebind action/button/dialog
  anywhere in web/src. An operator today cannot deliberately move a running
  case onto a different pinned version from the GUI at all, which is
  exactly the scenario's own step 5 action (with a caller-supplied reason
  -- `rebind_attrs()` requires `:idempotency_key`, per
  lib/letflow/routers/instances.ex's own design notes, and the scenario's
  step 5 input is `reason: \"External system retires the old endpoint at
  month end.\"`).
- Case history rendering: grepped web/src for any existing generic
  event-timeline renderer capable of showing an `INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND`
  entry with actor/prior_version/new_version/reason (EO-005's own evidence
  requirement, "the case history shows the change with the operator's
  name, the previous and new version, and the reason given") -- confirm at
  implementation time whether InstanceDetailPage.tsx's existing
  history/timeline section already renders arbitrary event types generically
  (in which case this requirement only needs the rebind action itself to
  produce the right event, already true by construction since
  `rebind_pins/3` already appends the real event) or needs a
  dedicated case for this event type -- do not assume either way without
  checking.

THIS REQUIREMENT BUILDS: (1) a typed `publish`/`retire` client pair in web/src/api/services.ts and UI controls on web/src/pages/admin/services/ServicesPage.tsx (a "publish new version" action taking the publish_attrs() fields plus a version string, and a "retire" action) for a PLATFORM_ADMIN-equivalent operator; (2) a typed `rebind` client function (POST /instances/:id/rebind-pins) and a rebind action/dialog on REQ-399's InstancePinsPanel.tsx (or InstanceDetailPage.tsx) requiring the caller to supply a reason string, wired to the real endpoint; (3) confirm, and if needed extend, the case history/timeline rendering so an `INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND` entry's actor, prior_version, new_version and reason are all visible per EO-005; (4) the named pipeline_test spec.
OUT OF SCOPE: any change to `Letflow.ServiceCatalog`, `PinResolver`, `PinRebind`, or any of REQ-373/REQ-399's already-shipped routes (pure frontend consumption/action wiring against already-shipped endpoints); re-scoping or modifying REQ-399's read-only provenance display beyond what is needed to add the rebind action to the same screen; PLC-01/module_ref catalog versioning (still the identical, already-named SCOPE GAP pin_resolver.ex's own moduledoc states, unscoped to any stage, restated by both REQ-373 and REQ-399).

task.description: WF-02 Step 2b (frontend implementation) for REQ-432. Step 2a (backend) is deliberately absent: this requirement is frontend-only and its OUT OF SCOPE clause forbids any change under lib/letflow/service_catalog*, lib/letflow/engine/pin_resolver.ex, pin_rebind.ex or any REQ-373/REQ-399 route -- do NOT touch anything under lib/. Verify branch feature/WF02-REQ432-20260930 first (git branch --show-current) else STOP and report FAIL before touching a file. Follow docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md Step 2b, .claude/agents/frontend-dev.md, docs/guides/frontend_developer_guide.md and web/README.md. The VALIDATED design is lib/letflow/design/req432-rebind-pins-publish-retire-ui.md (validated by handoffs/WF02-REQ432-20260930/step-01b-recheck1-code-design-validator.json); implement exactly that: sections 2/3 (publish/retire client + ServicesPage controls), 4/5 (rebind client, useRebindPins hook, rebind dialog on InstancePinsPanel, InstanceDetailPage wiring), 6 (PinsReboundSummary + EventHistoryPanel + page-level timeline join for actor name, EO-005 on ONE view), 7 (pipeline spec web/tests/e2e/pipelines/platform-instance-pin-survives-catalog-change.pipeline.e2e.spec.ts following the sibling specs' conventions, plus replacing the stale ISS-0527 NOTE in test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/platform/instance-pin-survives-catalog-change.yaml in the precedent style once the spec exists), 8 (unit/component tests for every acceptance criterion). Validator MINOR notes to honour: in the pipeline spec complete the n2 task with body {} (NOT {output_variables:{}}) because routers/tasks.ex passes the body itself as output_variables; copy the platform-definition-promotion-approved precedent node shape (label, attributes:null) exactly for the definition graph; capture the operator display name from the same timeline API response rather than hardcoding. Known backend limit (design M5, do not fix, do not shim): ServiceTaskDispatcher.catalog_lookup_stub/2 is unconditional {:error,:not_registered}, so the spec asserts the two designed step-3 outcomes and logs which occurred; this is to be reported in result.issues as MAJOR so ORCH can forward it. Other reported backend mismatches M1 (history_item_map omits actor_id), M2, M3: do not fix, do not shim; mention in result.issues only if your implementation hits them differently than the design states. Run the four gates from web/ and QUOTE the real output (final pass/fail counts): npm run type-check && npm run lint && npm test && npm run guards. Never weaken web/tests/guards/forbidlist.ts or add allowedPaths to pass a guard; if a guard blocks you, report it. PIPELINE SPEC EXECUTION: the acceptance criteria require the pipeline spec to pass. Docker services for this checkout (letflow-4-postgres-1, letflow-4-keycloak-1) are already running. Make a time-boxed, genuine attempt to run the new spec (npx playwright test <spec path>, see web/playwright.config.ts, web/tests/e2e/pipeline.ts header for required env like BPM_TEST_URL, scripts/uat_preflight.sh and docs/anti-patterns.md / docs/agents/protocols for how a local backend is started). If you can run it, quote the real result and fix failures (respecting the design). If you genuinely cannot bring up the backend/stack, STOP trying, do not fabricate a pass, run the spec at least through npx playwright test --list / type-check so it compiles, and report result.status PARTIAL with the exact reason and the exact command that would run it, leaving that one AC explicitly unverified. Run everything synchronously in the foreground (no background processes that outlive your turn; if you start a backend for the e2e run, stop it before finishing and confirm no orphan erl/beam/node processes remain -- see core-directives.md No Background Wait and ISS-0107). Never use directory junctions/symlinks for node_modules. Commit your work in logical commits by explicit filename (never git add -A) and push to origin feature/WF02-REQ432-20260930. Lint your handoff: mix letflow.lint_handoffs --dir handoffs/WF02-REQ432-20260930/step-02b-frontend-dev.json. Claim by setting status IN_PROGRESS only; on finish set COMPLETED/FAILED, fill result (artifacts_out: every file touched), real-clock completed_at; never edit task/created_at/started_at; do not write registry.json or orchestrator.log.
acceptance_criteria: type-check, lint, npm test and guards all pass with real output quoted
no guard weakened or exempted; no file under lib/ modified (git diff --name-only main...HEAD shows only web/, lib/letflow/design/, handoffs/, docs/ bookkeeping, and the scenario yaml)
publish and retire client functions call the real endpoints with the designed bodies; UI controls gated to PLATFORM_ADMIN; proven by unit tests
rebind requires a non-empty reason, sends Idempotency-Key, refetches pins; proven by tests
INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND history row shows operator name, prior version, new version and reason on one view; proven by tests
pipeline spec authored per design section 7 and either run green with real output quoted, or PARTIAL with exact blocker stated

result.summary: Implemented REQ-432 per the validated design: servicesApi.publishVersion/retire + PLATFORM_ADMIN-gated Publish/Retire controls and Version/Status columns on ServicesPage; instancesApi.rebindPins (Idempotency-Key header), useRebindPins (single instances.all() invalidation), rebind dialog on InstancePinsPanel (non-empty reason, changed version, key fresh per dialog open and reused on retry, gated by canRebind && instanceActive from InstanceDetailPage); PinsReboundSummary + EventHistoryPanel INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND rendering with the operator name joined page-side from the timeline feed (page_size 200) by event_id, so operator, prior version, new version and reason appear on ONE History row. Pipeline spec authored per design section 7 and the scenario yaml ISS-0527 NOTE replaced. Gates from web/ (real output): type-check clean; lint clean (--max-warnings 0); npm test 150 files / 994 tests passed; guards 4 files / 52 tests passed. 39 new unit/component tests across 8 files cover AC1-AC5. No file under lib/ changed (git diff --name-only main...HEAD outside web/, handoffs/, docs/ is only lib/letflow/design/req432-...md and the scenario yaml). PARTIAL: the pipeline spec compiles and lists (npx playwright test --list: 1 test) but could NOT be run green. Backend was brought up (MIX_ENV=dev with LETFLOW_DEV_DB_CONFIRMED=1 against this checkout's own Postgres on 5482, migrated; /api/v1/health answered 401 at 127.0.0.1:4000) but assertServiceReadiness failed with ECONNRESET on http://localhost:8094 (Keycloak): on this host localhost resolves to ::1 where wslrelay.exe (PID 21928) owns :8094 and resets connections, while Keycloak's docker port is reachable only via 127.0.0.1. The backend trusts issuer http://localhost:8094 (config/dev.exs) and helpers.ts normalises 127.0.0.1 to localhost, so tokens minted via 127.0.0.1 would carry a different issuer; no spec-side workaround is legitimate. Backend and Playwright-spawned dev server were stopped; no erl/node/listeners on 4000/4173 remain.

issues.description: AC6 half unverified: pipeline spec not run green. Blocker is host-environment, not code: http://localhost:8094 (Keycloak) is shadowed by wslrelay.exe on ::1, ECONNRESET in assertServiceReadiness. Command once fixed (backend: LETFLOW_SECRETS_MASTER_KEY from .env, LETFLOW_DEV_DB_CONFIRMED=1 MIX_ENV=dev mix run --no-halt): cd web && BPM_TEST_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4000 BPM_IDP_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8094 VITE_API_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4000 npx playwright test --config=playwright.config.ts tests/e2e/pipelines/platform-instance-pin-survives-catalog-change.pipeline.e2e.spec.ts. Selector assumptions in steps 02/07 (services list showing the new row without filtering, retired row still listed by /admin/services) are therefore also unproven live.

Design M5 (backend, not fixed, not shimmed): ServiceTaskDispatcher.catalog_lookup_stub/2 returns {:error,:not_registered} unconditionally, so a catalog SERVICE_TASK always ends EXECUTION_ERROR/request_build_error; the scenario's 'in-flight step completes without error' (EO-001/EO-004 step 3) cannot be met by the real backend. The spec asserts the two designed outcomes (SERVICE_TASK_COMPLETED or that exact EXECUTION_ERROR) and logs which occurred. Needs a REQ-ANALYST follow-on for the dispatcher to resolve service_id via the pinned catalog version.

Side effect for ORCH awareness: to attempt the e2e run I ran mix ecto.migrate against this checkout's dedicated Postgres (letflow-4-postgres-1, port 5482, letflow_dev) with LETFLOW_DEV_DB_CONFIRMED=1; that container is exclusive to this workspace per .env. No data was deliberately written.

Design M1/M2/M3 hit exactly as stated: history items omit actor_id (worked around only by the frontend event_id join for the rebound row, other rows still show 'system'); ServiceRecord max_retries/retry_policy not echoed; stale 'not permission-gated' moduledoc on rebind-pins. Not fixed.
